Submission: 10/26/2026

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • The purpose of this data sheet is to understand the thought process and the inner workings of the PCB board that connects all the other components in the Heart Rate Monitor project.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text: • The purpose of our project is to create a working heart rate monitoring system that will be displayed, as well as heard through speakers. The full report of the general workings of the heart rate monitor can be found here: team report.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
• The purpose of my PCB is to be the bridge between all other boards. My board will obtain the raw data from one of the boards, compile and simplify it, then send it out to the other two boards. Since my board will be connected to all others, a separate yet integrated temperature-sensing circuit has been added to indicate when the board gets too hot.
  • To review the general concept behind the design of the board, you can review it in the "Block Diagram" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the component selection process for the board, you can review it in the "Component Selection" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the bill of materials behind the chosen materials of the board, you can review it in the "BOM" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the schematic behind the design of the board, you can review it in the "Schematic" section of the datasheet.
  • To review the power budget, you can review it in the "Power Budget" section of the datasheet.

docs.title: Component Selection
docs.text:
Voltage Regulator

  1. Texas Instruments UA7805CKCS Voltage Regulator

    • $1.63/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Established 7805 style regulator design Linear regulator heat losses still apply Fixed 5 V output requires no output voltage adjustment Availability seems scarce Through hole versions are suitable for prototyping May cost more than other compatible options

  2. STMicroelectronics L7805BV Voltage Regulator

    • $1.53/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Provides fixed 5 V suitable for Curiosity Nano and MCP6004 Needs an input voltage above 5 V, with sufficient headroom. Through-hole TO-220 package is relatively easy to solder Excess input voltage is dissipated as heat. Includes overtemperature and short-circuit protection The 1.5 A rating does not guarantee that it can deliver 1.5 A continuously without appropriate thermal management.

  3. NTE960 Voltage Regulator

    • $1.50/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Fixed 5 V output May not deliver consistent 1 A according to reviews Through-hole package is convenient for assembly Releases more heat than other similar components Its 1 A output rating may be sufficient for a modest logic board Better choices for a similar price Choice: Option 2: STMicroelectronics L7805BV Voltage Regulator

Rationale: The L7805BV was selected for its fixed 5 V output. Its simple design makes it easy to integrate into the PCB. Its through-hole package also makes assembly easier, and I already own the component.

External Power Supply

  1. WALL ADAPTER 9VDC 1A, 5.5X2.1MM External Power Supply

    • $11.41/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Supplies up to 1 A at 9 V A linear 5 V regulator will dissipate substantial heat dropping 9 V to 5 V Convenient for a stationary prototype The adapter's connector might not fit perfectly with the preferred jack; it might work with a backup. Provides more input voltage than a 5 V rail requires Its current capacity must be checked against the calculated system load

  2. Avue 12V, 1 A Adapter External Power Supply

    • $9.99/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons A readily purchasable wall adapter. Same linear regulator heat concern as option 1. Rated for 12 W of output power. The connector and polarity must be verified. Suitable for evaluating a stationary prototype if the connector and electrical specifications match. Must have sufficient current remaining after accounting for all loads.

  3. Triad Magnetics AC/DC WALL MOUNT ADAPTER 9V 12W External Power Supply

    • $7.99/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Supplies 9 V DC and is intended for continuous equipment power. The jack's inner diameter is 2.0 mm, while the adapter plug is listed as 2.1 mm. Lower input voltage than 12 V reduces the regulator's voltage drop and heat. Its center-negative connector may not match the barrel jack. Listed output current is 1.3 A. A linear regulator will still dissipate heat, and the actual current demand must be calculated.

Choice: Option 1: WALL ADAPTER 9VDC 1A, 5.5X2.1MM External Power Supply

Rationale: The 9 V adapter was selected because it provides a practical power source for a stationary prototype. It produces less heat than a 12 V adapter with a linear regulator. It can provide consistent power without requiring a battery. Its polarity and connector match one of the two potential jacks.

Op Amp

  1. Microchip Technology MCP6004-I/P Op Amp

    • $0.60/each
    • link to product
    Pros Cons Low power consumption: Typical supply current is about 100 µA. Its switching behavior may be less predictable than a comparator designed for threshold detection. Already in Possession Its 1 MHz gain bandwidth makes it unsuitable for some high-speed applications. Rail-to-rail input-to-output Can be easily damaged

  2. Texas Instruments LM324N Op amp

    • $0.58/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Works with 5V supply Output does not reach the positive supply rail. Easy to socket and replace Higher supply current than the MCP6004. Four amplifier sections in one chip Not a dedicated comparator; switching behavior needs testing.

Choice: Option 1: Microchip Technology MCP6004-I/P Op Amp

Rationale: Microchip Technology MCP6004-I/P Op Amp will be chosen due to the component already being in my possession. MCP6004 also attaches well to the PCB's 5V rail, and I already know the op-amp works.

Power Jack

  1. Texas Instruments PJ-002AH Power Jack

    • $0.81/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Designed for standard 5.5 x 2.1 mm DC plugs. Limited Insertion life. Through-hole terminals Requires the jack to be positioned at the PCB edge. Solderable pins make PCB connection easy The jack itself does not ensure center-positive wiring.

  2. Texas Instruments PJ-102AH Power Jack

    • $0.83/each
    • Link to product
    Pros Cons Comfortably supports 5A Its 2.0 mm center pin size may not fit a 2.1 mm. Already in possession. Requires careful placement on PCB edge. Has a normally closed internal switch contact. Polarity is not enforced.

Choice: Option 1: Texas Instruments PJ-102AH Power Jack

Rationale: Texas Instruments PJ-102AH Power Jack was chosen because it is already in my possession and may work with my backup wall power adapter. If the selected power jack does not work, I will order the other one as a backup to ensure a component malfunction does not play a bigger role in the project delay.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is designed to support team 204's Heart Rate Monitor. Its purpose is to receive and compile information, then send it to two other PCBs. The Board shall consist of three different circuits. The first circuit is responsible for supplying power, with a blue LED indicating whether the power is on. The second circuit involves the microcontroller, and it will receive an analog signal from one board and send it to the other two boards. Finally, the third circuit is responsible for measuring the board's temperature and lighting a red LED if it gets too hot.
